title: Organic SEO
summary: The non-map side of search: page structure, useful content, and technical fixes so the site can rank beyond the listing.
metaTitle: Organic SEO for Local Businesses | Nick Perry Digital
metaDescription: Organic SEO for Western Slope service businesses: site structure, content, and technical fixes, paired with local search work.
body:
Organic SEO is the work on your website that helps ordinary Google results, not only the map. A strong listing can bring calls while the site still fails to explain a service or load cleanly on a phone.

On a monthly plan this shows up as on-site updates, new or revised pages, and technical fixes. It is also part of the 90 days after a website build. I write for the services and towns you named. I do not publish filler articles to hit a word count.
gets: A look at titles, headings, and internal links
Pages that answer the questions customers already ask
Technical fixes that affect indexing and speed
Content updates tied to services you want to sell
Notes in the monthly report on what changed and why

steps.title: Read the site
steps.text: I review what already ranks, what is thin, and which services have no page at all.

steps.title: Fix the important pages
steps.text: Service pages, the homepage, and town pages come before a blog burst.

steps.title: Add proof over time
steps.text: New pages and edits follow the jobs you want. Each month the report says what was published.

faqs.q: How is organic SEO different from local SEO?
faqs.a: Local SEO leans on the Google listing, the map, and town relevance. Organic SEO leans on the website itself. You usually need both.

faqs.q: Will you write a blog post every week?
faqs.a: Only if it helps. A useless post is not a strategy. The monthly plans include content, and I will tell you what I am writing before it goes live.

faqs.q: Is this included in the $850 plan?
faqs.a: Yes. On-site SEO, content updates, and conversion edits are in both monthly plans. The $1,500 plan adds AI search work and local outreach on top.

faqs.q: Can organic SEO fix a slow or broken site?
faqs.a: Some fixes are part of the work. If the site needs to be rebuilt, that is the website build or a custom quote, not a blog calendar.
